findings.title: Post-lock validation still accepts a merge in lockedStartingHead..baseline
findings.claim: Candidate 3 fixes full-history lane-path traversal and makes the lock creator reject prebaseline merges, but the independent post-lock validator does not enforce the same linear-history contract. A manually constructed, otherwise creator-equivalent direct-child lock on a merge baseline passes the complete public post-lock validator with zero failures when the merge contains no lane artifact. Thus later validation cannot prove that the reviewed baseline was reached by the required linear prebaseline chain; it relies on the one-time creator having been used honestly.
evidence: scripts/create_correctness_audit_lock.py:101-117 now uses git log --full-history, so a lane artifact introduced/deleted on a merged side branch is detected.
scripts/create_correctness_audit_lock.py:120-130 detects merges in lockedStartingHead..baseline, and lines 195-199 invoke that check in the creator.
scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:39-42 imports historical_lane_files and required_locked_files but not starting_head_failures.

scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:531-552 rejects merges only in baseline..HEAD, then checks starting-head ancestry and historical lane paths; it never rejects merge commits in lockedStartingHead..baseline.

findings.reproduction: Run the saved bounded candidate3_postlock_e2e_probe.py through the pinned audit uv environment. It clones exact candidate 6a13b9e6f57307a76756cf90da2aaa7682aa699b into a temporary repository, hardlinks and byte-preserves the 1,098 gitignored source files, creates a no-content prebaseline side commit and a two-parent merge baseline, manually writes the exact creator-format lock with the complete required locked-file hash map, commits that lock as the baseline's immediate direct child, and calls validate_correctness_audit.validate(require_lock=True). The creator helper rejects the merge, but the complete post-lock validator returns passed=true with zero failures and the clone remains clean.
findings.recommendation: Make post-lock validate_lock enforce the same starting-head contract as the creator, preferably by importing and applying starting_head_failures(lockedStartingHead, baseline) or by directly rejecting any git rev-list --merges lockedStartingHead..baseline result. Add an end-to-end post-lock negative control whose otherwise valid direct-child lock sits on a merge baseline and require the complete validator to fail.

residualRisks: Candidate 3 is intentionally prelock and has no real 140-unit post-lock lane graph. WAVE-001 was verified with exact-candidate committed temporary histories, the 92-test suite, and the validator's global commit-set gate, not with production audit artifacts.

The end-to-end PROV-002 attack manually creates the lock only after confirming the official creator rejects the merge. This is the relevant adversarial boundary: post-lock validation must independently reject an invalid but internally consistent committed lock topology.

No additional provenance or wave defect was reproduced. Post-seal full-history mutation rejection, creator-side prebaseline merge rejection, prebaseline full-history lane detection, per-lane dependency ordering, and common wave-commit cardinality all held in executed controls.
